definitions.definition: For each nonnegative integer k, Eucl(k)=R^k is the space of real k-tuples, with distance (sum_{j=1}^k |x_j-y_j|^2)^(1/2) and its Borel sigma algebra. The empty tuple is the sole point of Eucl(0). Eucl(k)×R is identified with Eucl(k+1) by adjoining the last coordinate; this identification uses the Euclidean distance sqrt(||x-y||_2^2+|t-u|^2).

definitions.type: diameter function on subsets of metric or extended metric spaces
definitions.definition: diam(A)=sup{dist(x,y): x,y in A}, as an extended nonnegative number, with supremum of the empty set zero. Thus diam(empty)=0. In ordinary Euclidean spaces a nonempty set of diameter zero is a singleton. Native ediam is this extended-valued diameter. Euclidean finite diameters are identified with their nonnegative real values.

binders.type: subset of a metric or extended metric space

definitions.type: positive exponent and scale Hausdorff contents and limiting Hausdorff measure on Euclidean sets
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of the same Euclidean space

definitions.type: real exponent → Borel Hausdorff measure on any extended metric space
definitions.definition: muH(a) denotes the native unnormalized Borel Hausdorff measure MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a. It is obtained by the metric outer-measure construction mkMetric with gauge r↦r^a on extended nonnegative diameters: at each positive scale take the maximal outer measure bounded by the gauge on all nonempty sets of at most that diameter, then take the supremum over scales and its Borel-measure realization. Values on arbitrary sets mean outer-measure values. Empty covering members cost zero and nonempty members cost diam^a with extended nonnegative-real powers; at a=0 a nonempty singleton has cost 1.

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of subsets of metric spaces, valued in [0,infinity]
definitions.definition: dimH(A), also written dim_H A, is the standard Hausdorff dimension: sup({a≥0 : muH(a)(A)=infinity}) in [0,infinity], where the supremum of an empty set is 0. This is the native dimH definition. The notation uses the empty-set dimension convention 0. Critical-exponent properties and agreement with the supplied positive-exponent diameter-cost measure are proof obligations, not extra assumptions.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.definition: F=E×I under the Euclidean identification in D001.
D=dimH(E), initially an extended nonnegative real. Real arithmetic involving D is used only after its finiteness is proved.

inputs.statement: For every nonnegative integer k, every A⊆Eucl(k), and every real a>0, H^a(A)=muH(a)(A). Consequently: a>dimH(A) implies H^a(A)=0; 0<a<dimH(A) implies H^a(A)=infinity; H^a(A)=0 implies dimH(A)≤a; and H^a(A)=infinity implies dimH(A)≥a. Hausdorff dimension is nonnegative. For A⊆B⊆Eucl(k), dimH(A)≤dimH(B). For every nonnegative integer l and every distance-preserving map g:A→Eucl(l), dimH(g(A))=dimH(A).

argument.text: H002 supplies a point x0∈E. Define g:I→Eucl(n+1) by g(t)=(x0,t). The Euclidean distance between g(t) and g(u) is sqrt(0+|t-u|^2)=|t-u|, so g preserves distances. Its image is contained in F by x0∈E and the definition F=E×I. N001 gives dimH(g(I))=dimH(I) and dimH(F)≥dimH(g(I)). N006 gives dimH(I)=1, hence dimH(F)≥1. Under the temporary premise L1: D=0, this reads dimH(F)≥1=D+1. Discharge L1; x0 is absent from the output. This proves the exported claim for all n, including n=0.
